slides.title: ODD+LLM: Specifying LLM-Agent Behavior for Reproducible Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces ODD+LLM, an extension to the ODD protocol that standardizes the documentation of LLM-agent components like prompt assembly and memory serialization, addressing significant reproducibility gaps in social simulations.

card.one_liner: ODD+LLM extends the ODD protocol to standardize LLM-agent behavior specifications for reproducible social simulations.
card.key_idea: Adds five documentation blocks (CoALA-based) covering prompt assembly, memory, parsing, and retry logic to the existing ODD framework.
card.evaluation: Multiverse analysis of a naming-game simulation and a review of 28 papers showing 77% of prompt/parsing details are undetermined.
card.limitation: Single-case demonstration; assumes text-in/text-out models; does not guarantee reproducibility due to inherent model stochasticity.

slides.title: AVCC: Audio-Visual Conversation Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction with a Human Benchmark
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a public benchmark for next-speaker prediction using a single static camera and microphone, directly addressing the sensor constraints relevant to HyECHO's goal of modeling hybrid human-AI team state in realistic settings.

card.one_liner: AVCC provides a single-camera audio-visual benchmark for multiparty turn-taking prediction with human baselines.
card.key_idea: Constructs a 31-hour corpus from online videos with one static camera/mic, adding speaker-disjoint test partitions, transcripts, and human reference data.
card.evaluation: Scored RoleVAP and MuVAP models against 154 human participants on 1,730 events using balanced accuracy for hold/shift and next-speaker prediction.
card.limitation: Human observers lacked access to cues within the silence gap, potentially underestimating performance on short gaps compared to models.

slides.title: Rhythmic-Semantic Co-Speech Gestures for Emotional Dialogue in Robots
slides.highlight: This work presents a system that generates both rhythmic and semantic co-speech gestures based on emotional state, deployed on the Haru social robot to improve engagement and speech understanding.

card.one_liner: Emotion-aware system generates rhythmic and semantic co-speech gestures for robots using text-only input.
card.key_idea: Lightweight BERT/RoBERTa models predict iconic gesture timing/intensity and beat intensity from text and emotion, merging them into real-time robot motion.
card.evaluation: Trained on BEAT2; deployed on Haru robot. Online study (N=60) showed higher speech-gesture correlation and preference over LLM/random baselines.
card.limitation: Text-only inference ignores prosody; relies on predefined iconic animation libraries; evaluated only on non-anthropomorphic robot via video.

slides.title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that conventional acoustic features and self-supervised speech representations can effectively classify speaker familiarity and kinship in dyadic conversations, offering a non-data-hungry approach to inferring social relationships from audio.

card.one_liner: Acoustic features classify speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations, outperforming LLMs and humans.
card.key_idea: Compares five speech representations (spectral, WavLM, x-vectors, articulatory) using ResNet/SVM classifiers with conversation-level aggregation.
card.evaluation: Tested on Seamless Interaction corpus; spectral features best for familiarity, WavLM/x-vectors for kinship, exceeding LLM/human baselines.
card.limitation: Single dataset with few test dyads, class imbalance in kinship, and lack of explicit modeling for turn-taking or temporal dynamics.

slides.title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
slides.tldr: THEORY OF MIND FOR LLM TEACHING
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how Theory of Mind principles can enable stronger LLMs to effectively teach fixed-student agents by modeling their limitations and transferring reusable skills, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that infer partner intent and adapt at test time.

card.one_liner: Student-Aware Teaching improves LLM agent success by modeling learner limitations to write targeted, reusable skills.
card.key_idea: Teacher builds a learner model, uses diagnostic probes to identify execution constraints, and admits skills only if they improve development task success.
card.evaluation: Claude-Sonnet-5 taught DeepSeek-V4-Flash on five task suites; SAT achieved 86.46% success, outperforming agnostic teaching (81.04%) and untaught baselines.
card.limitation: Benefit requires students capable of following instructions; gains diminish for very small models or those already near performance ceiling.

slides.title: Xinhua Unveils Bionic Humanoid Robot News Anchors with UBTECH
slides.highlight: The deployment of bionic humanoid robots as news anchors highlights advancements in embodied social presence and human-robot interaction, relevant to the development of socially capable robots.

slides.title: Xinhua launches world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchors
slides.highlight: Xinhua has introduced bionic humanoid robots as news anchors, demonstrating advanced human-robot interaction and embodied presence in media contexts.

slides.title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a framework for configuring and observing LLM-agent teams using human-team theory, offering a structured approach to modeling team dynamics and intervention points relevant to hybrid human-AI team state perception.

card.one_liner: Teamknitt is a framework for configuring, observing, and intervening in LLM-agent teams using human-team theory.
card.key_idea: Explicitly configures team topology, sharing profiles, and bindings, enabling human-led interventions and dual-perspective observation of agent interactions.
card.evaluation: System description and reference implementation only; no comparative results reported, though falsifiable hypotheses and offline demonstrations are provided.
card.limitation: Does not measure emergent psychological states like trust or cohesion; relies on human-led interventions without automated organizational optimization.

slides.title: Pandemonium: Longform Target-Speaker Speech Recognition with Cross-Speaker Interactions
slides.highlight: This paper introduces cross-speaker attention in longform target-speaker ASR, enabling models to attend across speaker dimensions rather than decoding in isolation, which directly supports HyECHO's goal of modeling hybrid human-AI team state and interactions.

card.one_liner: Pandemonium achieves state-of-the-art longform target-speaker ASR via cross-speaker attention and pseudo-labeled data.
card.key_idea: Integrates diarization conditioning into a longform Parakeet backbone, adding cross-speaker attention and an STNO mask refiner to model speaker interactions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NSF, AMI, ICSI, Mx6, SBC, and DiPCo using cpWER; outperforms DiCoW baselines with oracle and predicted diarization.
card.limitation: Relies on external diarization accuracy; CTC training incurs slight accuracy loss compared to TDT; pseudo-labels contain residual noise.

slides.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
slides.tldr: GENEA MODEL FOR EMBODIED PLAN REASONING
slides.highlight: The GenEA framework demonstrates how generative models of embodied plans can accurately recapitulate human reasoning about goals and actions, offering a potential architecture for social robots to interpret human intentions.

card.one_liner: GenEA, a generative model coupling biomechanics with intuitive physics, accurately predicts human reasoning about embodied plans.
card.key_idea: Extends task-and-motion planning with a dynamics level simulating intuitive physics, creating a multilevel state-space for generative reasoning over long-horizon embodied actions.
card.evaluation: Tested against humans and baselines (TAMP, heuristics, VLMs) in manipulation and navigation tasks; GenEA showed high correlation with human judgments and response times.
card.limitation: Relies on predefined symbolic action primitives and coarse biomechanical models, potentially limiting generalization to highly complex or novel physical interactions.

slides.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how Theory of Mind reasoning and communication theory can be leveraged to detect deception in multi-agent settings, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of inferring partner intent and maintaining alignment in human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AVCORP uses a deception corpus and Theory of Mind reasoning to train LLM detectors that outperform frontier models.
card.key_idea: Constructs a 5,000-utterance corpus from Avalon games with tactic labels and nested Theory of Mind reasoning traces to fine-tune Qwen3-8B for deception detection.
card.evaluation: Tested on held-out synthetic games and human Avalon-NLU games; trained detector matches Claude Opus 5.5 and beats GPT-5.6 Sol on exact match.
card.limitation: Relies on synthetic dialogue lacking human nuances; training uses gold prior traces, creating a mismatch with self-generated traces at inference.

slides.title: Off-target posterior mass: A training-free diagnostic for fine-tuning spoken language diarization probes
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Off-target Posterior Mass (OTPM), a training-free metric to predict performance gains in Spoken Language Diarization (SLD) fine-tuning, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of efficient multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: OTPM predicts spoken language diarization fine-tuning gains without training or labels.
card.key_idea: Measures posterior mass assigned to non-target languages in pre-trained models to forecast probe gains via linear regression.
card.evaluation: Tested on synthetic FLEURS and real SEAME/VoxPopuli/DISPLACE corpora; Spearman correlations range from 0.23 to 0.69.
card.limitation: Weak generalization to real-world data due to synthetic-to-real distribution shifts and unmodeled target-language confusion.

slides.title: ReSUM: Reasoning-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Query-Focused Summarization
slides.highlight: ReSUM addresses the challenges of complex speaker dynamics and sparse key information in long meetings through a modular multi-LLM framework, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI team settings.

card.one_liner: ReSUM uses a multi-agent framework with reasoning distillation to improve query-focused meeting summarization.
card.key_idea: Decouples tasks into planner, retriever, summarizer, and critique agents, using teacher LLM chain-of-thought distillation for smaller models.
card.evaluation: Tested on QMSum and SQuALITY against zero-shot, CoT, RAG, and fine-tuned baselines using ROUGE, BERTScore, and human evaluation.
card.limitation: Computational overhead from multiple agents and iterative critique loops; reliance on strong teacher LLMs for generating reasoning traces.

slides.title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how a world model can learn unseen game mechanics through test-time parameter updates, directly supporting ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that adapt beyond in-context learning by inferring environmental rules from limited interactions.

card.one_liner: World models learn unseen game mechanics in ~80 exposures via test-time gradient updates.
card.key_idea: WARC, a 35M vision transformer, updates all parameters after each transition to learn new game mechanics from limited exposures.
card.evaluation: MechEval on ARC-AGI-3 (69 mechanics, 20 games); WARC-Agent triples explorer efficiency score vs baselines.
card.limitation: Results limited to deterministic, discrete grid games; unclear if effective for continuous or stochastic dynamics.

slides.title: Beyond the Transcript: Measuring and Improving the Use of Acoustic Information in Audio Language Models
slides.tldr: IMPROVING ACOUSTIC INFORMATION USAGE IN AUDIO LMS
slides.highlight: This work addresses the confounding of language modeling and acoustic understanding in audio models, demonstrating that targeted training can significantly improve the extraction of paralinguistic cues like emotion and speaker identity from recordings. This is relevant to HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry multimodal social perception, as it offers a method to enhance the model's ability to interpret global attributes and within-recording structures essential for understanding hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: Audio LLMs underuse acoustic cues already encoded in early layers; targeted LoRA training fixes this gap.
card.key_idea: Identify layers where acoustic readout declines, train LoRA adapters there with a content anchor to improve paralinguistic understanding without harming lexical accuracy.
card.evaluation: Tested 19 open models and Gemini on 92 tasks; linear probes confirmed information presence; LoRA repair raised attribute/structure accuracy by 12-44pp.
card.limitation: Repair validated on only two models; synthetic reading references may introduce bias; transfer to unseen task formats remains inconsistent.

slides.title: Perception, Not Reasoning, Limits Visual Theory of Mind
slides.highlight: This study identifies perceptual scene-state extraction, rather than reasoning modules, as the primary bottleneck for visual Theory of Mind in vision-language models, directly informing ADAM-CHAT's need for robust intent inference in visual environments.

card.one_liner: Visual Theory of Mind failures stem from perceptual bottlenecks, not reasoning deficits.
card.key_idea: Five-condition dissociation protocol varying perceptual fidelity to isolate scene-state extraction as the primary bottleneck.
card.evaluation: Seven VLMs on abstract/naturalistic scenes via 159k API calls; ground-truth scaffolds close gaps, automatic parsers fail.
card.limitation: Relies on oracle scaffolds; automatic parsers remain insufficient, leaving practical visual extraction unsolved.

slides.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
slides.highlight: Sage-Taiyi demonstrates that explicit monitoring and control of evidence and assumptions can effectively guide research targets and reasoning methods, offering a concrete implementation of metacognitive self-correction relevant to ADAM-CHAT's goal of AI teammates that adapt and self-monitor.

card.one_liner: Sage-Taiyi uses metacognitive monitoring to guide scientific ideation, outperforming baselines on Taiyi-Bench.
card.key_idea: A two-level architecture where meta-level monitoring updates a cognitive state to regulate object-level search targets and method selection.
card.evaluation: Ranked first on all 8 Taiyi-Bench metrics (Overall 54.0 vs 47.9 baseline) and validated via expert-guided chemistry experiments.

slides.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
slides.tldr: MECHANICAL VALIDITY INSUFFICIENT FOR LLM WORLD MODELS
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that LLM-generated world models, while often mechanically valid, frequently lack the structural fidelity required for reliable neuro-symbolic reasoning, a critical challenge for MIMIC's agent-based simulations.

card.one_liner: Mechanically valid LLM-generated world models often lack structural fidelity, risking errors in downstream safety reasoning.
card.key_idea: Evaluates LLM-generated Partially Observable Stochastic Games via mechanical validity, structural agreement with references, and semantic checks.
card.evaluation: 44 scenarios across game, situational, and cultural tracks; 410 generations from five LLMs; metrics include structural F1 and mechanical pass rates.
card.limitation: Small hand-crafted benchmark; structural comparison limited to depth three; human semantic validation incomplete; no downstream planning impact measured.

slides.title: Adaptive Residual Quantization for Memory-Efficient Temporal Action Segmentation
slides.tldr: COMPACT LABEL-FREE MEMORY FOR TEMPORAL ACTION SEGMENTATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces ARQ-VAE, a compact, label-free memory representation for temporal action segmentation that reduces storage needs while mitigating catastrophic forgetting in incremental settings. It is relevant to MOSAIC as it offers a scalable solution for retaining procedural skill data across long-form video tasks without requiring dense frame-wise annotations.

card.one_liner: ARQ-VAE compresses TAS features 2800x by adaptively truncating residual codes per frame, preserving segmentation accuracy.
card.key_idea: Trains a fixed-depth RQ-VAE, then adaptively truncates residual code prefixes per frame based on reconstruction error, followed by decoder fine-tuning.
card.evaluation: Tested on GTEA, 50Salads, Breakfast, and YTI using MS-TCN/ASFormer; outperforms TCA/GNI baselines in storage-performance trade-off across supervised/incremental settings.
card.limitation: Requires pre-extracted frame features and a two-stage training process (full RQ-VAE then fine-tuning), adding complexity compared to simple quantization.

slides.title: Meta Acquires Conductor to Support Multi-Agent AI Coding
slides.highlight: Meta's acquisition of Conductor to support multi-agent AI coding highlights the growing industrial focus on coordinating autonomous agents, a key challenge in modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

slides.title: Where to Approximate in Neurosymbolic Inference?
slides.highlight: This work improves the scalability of neurosymbolic inference by optimizing approximation strategies in weighted model counting, directly supporting MIMIC's goal of modeling complex human-AI interactions through efficient symbolic-logical reasoning.

card.one_liner: Tensor train-based pipelines improve neurosymbolic inference accuracy by preserving factor dependencies during compilation.
card.key_idea: Unifies approximate compilation into three stages, using tensor train decompositions for factor approximation and SVD-based recompression during multiplication.
card.evaluation: Tested on Sudoku, arithmetic, and scene understanding tasks; achieves orders-of-magnitude lower WMC error than fuzzy baselines with better learning outcomes.
card.limitation: Requires careful tuning of ranks and multiplication schedules; excessive recompression can degrade representation despite good aggregate error metrics.

slides.title: Koopman Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Koopman model-based reinforcement learning algorithm that simplifies policy gradient computation for nonlinear robotic systems, offering a computationally efficient approach to control that could enhance the adaptive AI coaching components of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: K-MBRL uses linear Koopman models and one-step predictions for efficient, real-time control of nonlinear robots.
card.key_idea: Learns dynamics via deep Koopman operators for linear policy gradients, combining immediate costs with critic-estimated future costs at one-step predicted states.
card.evaluation: Validated on HalfCheetah, quadruped simulations, and physical bipedal walking; outperforms model-free and standard model-based RL baselines in sample efficiency.
card.limitation: Relies on fixed-dataset convergence assumptions and requires sufficient data richness for accurate Koopman lifting and critic estimation.
